title: Affine triple slices of an oriented product have finite-cover presentations
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use their small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and form the left oriented product $P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$ on the triple site $\mathcal C$ of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Let $Z=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ be an object of $\mathcal C$ with $U,V,W$ affine. Let $H_Z=h_Z^\#$ be its associated representable sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and write $P/H_Z$ for the category of objects of $P$ equipped with a morphism to $H_Z$. The slice projection $j_Z:P/H_Z\to P$ has inverse image $F\mapsto(F\times H_Z\to H_Z)$.

There is a canonical equivalence over $P$
$$P/H_Z\simeq U_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{V_{\mathrm{Et}}}W_{\mathrm{Et}},$$
where the two scheme morphisms are the arrows $U\to V$ and $W\to V$ of $Z$. Under this equivalence $j_Z$ is the morphism induced by $U\to X$, $V\to S$, $W\to Y$ and their commutativities. Because $U,V,W$ are affine, the restricted scheme morphisms are quasi-compact and the corresponding small etale topoi are coherent. The topos on the right therefore has a small site $\mathcal D_Z$ in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention] with finite limits, every covering of which admits a finite covering refinement. One may take a small skeleton of the triples $(U'\to V'\leftarrow W')$ in which $U'\to U$, $V'\to V$ and $W'\to W$ are affine etale objects, with the oriented-product topology generated by finite families of types (a), (b) and singleton families of type (c) in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. For a sheaf of sets $F$ on $\mathcal C$, the corresponding restriction $j_Z^{-1}F$ has global sections canonically $F(Z)$.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.10(b), equivalence (1.b) and localization (1.c), printed pp. 175–176 (PDF pp. 181–182); the finite-cover pretopology is the construction in the proof of Lemma 2.5, printed pp. 179–180 (PDF pp. 185–186), applied to the coherent small etale sites of affine U,V,W and their quasi-compact induced morphisms.

proof.text: Apply the canonical localization theorem for an oriented product at a representable triple. For the given $Z$, it identifies the slice $P/H_Z$ over $P$ with $U_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{V_{\mathrm{Et}}}W_{\mathrm{Et}}$, and identifies the projection $j_Z$ with the morphism induced by the three structure maps and their commutativity.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.10(b), equivalence (1.b) and localization (1.c), printed pp. 175–176 (PDF pp. 181–182)

proof.text: Use the affine étale sites on $U$, $V$, and $W$. The affine-site equivalence and the cover-dense essentially small affine basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos, lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover] allow a small skeleton of triples $(U'\to V'\leftarrow W')$ with all three objects affine and étale over $U,V,W$. Fiber products of affine schemes over an affine scheme are affine [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and étale morphisms are stable under base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; hence the three affine étale sites have finite limits (the final objects $U,V,W$ are affine), the functors $V'\mapsto U\times_VV'$ and $V'\mapsto W\times_VV'$ preserve them and send standard étale coverings to standard étale coverings, and the triple category built on these sites has componentwise finite limits. Morphisms between affine schemes are quasi-compact. The standard étale coverings on each affine factor are finite families; the oriented-product pretopology generated by the two factor covering types and the singleton base-change type is stable under pullback, and every generated covering is a finite composite. Hence every covering admits a finite covering refinement, so every object is quasi-compact; this is the coherence of the restricted affine étale topoi and of the slice. Finally, the affine sites satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] (small, finite limits, pretopologies, finite-limit-preserving continuous inverse images), so its independence clause identifies the sheaf topos on this triple site $\mathcal D_Z$ with $U_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{V_{\mathrm{Et}}}W_{\mathrm{Et}}$, the oriented product built from the full small étale sites; this gives the asserted small site $\mathcal D_Z$.

source.place: Exposé XI 2.5, printed pp. 179–180 (PDF pp. 185–186), applied to the affine étale sites; the finite-cover construction is the proof of Lemma 2.5

proof.text: In the slice topos, the inverse image of $F$ is $(F\times H_Z\to H_Z)$. A global section over the terminal slice object is therefore a morphism over $H_Z$ from $H_Z$ to $F\times H_Z$, equivalently a morphism $H_Z\to F$ in $P$. By the sheafification adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], morphisms $H_Z=h_Z^\#$ to $F$ are canonically identified with $F(Z)$. This identification is natural in $F$, proving $\Gamma(P/H_Z,j_Z^{-1}F)\cong F(Z)$.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.10(b), the localization slice and representable evaluation; Yoneda/sheafification adjunction supplies the section formula

proof_origin.place: Exposé XI 1.10(b), 2.5 and the proof of Lemma 2.5, printed pp. 175–176 and 179–180 (PDF pp. 181–182 and 185–186)
